note: Append-only fly-shop calibration log. One record = one shop report for one river on one day. Never overwrite; each scrape appends. PULL-AND-PARK: the scraper collects ALL rivers a shop offers, but off-gauge rivers (no gauge in this app yet) are parked with gauges:[] and active:false -- collected + dated from day one so future drainages (e.g. Clark Fork incl. Rock Creek) start with banked history. Activating later = fill gauges[] + flip active:true; no re-scrape, no reformat. Active queries filter active:true. Fly table primary; tip prose cross-checks. Ratings normalized to 0-10 (rating.value0to10). Shop water temp is SOFT cross-check only -- our gauges authoritative. nameCanonical (alias layer, build-step 1) drives cross-shop agreement counting.

schema.scrapedAt: ISO datetime -- when WE pulled it
schema.source: platform (Orvis, Grizzly Hackle, Fly Fish Food, Blackfoot-own)
schema.reporter: the actual guide/shop author -- weighting is by this, not source
schema.gauges: array of our gauge ids this report covers (crosswalk to the app)
schema.flies: array of { rank, nameRaw, nameCanonical, type(dry|nymph|dd|streamer), colors[], sizes }
schema.tipFlies: array of fly names pulled from the tip prose (cross-check)
schema.drainage: drainage key (e.g. 'bitterroot','clark-fork') -- groups rivers for future multi-drainage expansion
schema.active: bool -- true if this river maps to a live gauge in THIS app; false = parked (collected but not in the active dataset)

reports.technique: A dry-dropper rig is the best option to cover water. Throw a Chubby Chernobyl or Water Walker and then drop a PMD nymph or a general attractor nymph like a Blowtorch, Duracell, or Frenchie 18 to 24 inches below the dry. As the hatches of PMDs and Caddis happen throughout the entire day look for rising fish and switch over to a single dry. A Purple Haze, Hot Spot Para-Wulff, a PMD spinner or a small Elk Hair Caddis are great options to catch those rising fish.
reports.tip: The Bitterroot is taking its summer fishing shape. Riffle edges, tailouts, grassy banks, and soft bank seams are absolutely loaded with feeding fish. The trout are seeing a variety of bugs, making them active and willing to eat dry flies. Log jams and debris are still a major hazard especially with the watering dropping as fast as it is, so floaters need to stay alert. Float cautiously! Fishing in the morning and the evenings will be the best time to be on the water. Keep an eye on water temps in the afternoons as it is starting to get hotter.

reports.tip: Closed to floating from Weigh Station Fishing Access Site downstream to the point where the river crosses under Interstate 90, beginning July 15 due to construction on a railway bridge. The Blackfoot is fishing well with cooler water. Target deep pools, heavy shaded runs, and fast inside bank seams. Later in the afternoon fish shaded areas and deep pools where fish can get away from the sun. ***There is an obstruction below Harry Morgan on the North Fork of the Blackfoot that has caused a few boat accidents. We recommend either walking your boat around it or putting in at River Junction instead***

reports.technique: Start with a size #12–#14 Hopper, Foam Beetle, or Chubby along the shaded banks. If trout aren't fully committing to the dry fly, tie a dropper on like size #14–#16 Perdigon, Duracell, or Jigged Hare’s Ear dropped 2 feet underneath.
reports.tip: Rock Creek is in great late season wading shape with cold, clear water moving through. Terrestrials along the grassy willow margins remain a great way to attract fish. Focus your attention on shaded pocket water, fast boulder seams, and deep riffle transitions. ***Closed to fishing from boats/vessels July 1 through Nov. 30***

reports.technique: A dry-dropper rig is a great way to attract fish. Tie on a Chubby Chernobyl, More or Less Hopper, or a foam hopper on top, and trail a nymph like a Frenchie, Duracell, or Black Spanish Bullet 3 to 4 feet underneath. Be on the lookout for tricos hatching and fish sipping them on the surface. Streamer fishing is also a great way to move fish with the cooler weather.
reports.tip: The Clark Fork is fishing very well right now. Fish the grassy banks with a hopper. Trout will hide along shallow bank edges, sweepers, and eddy lines to grab hoppers, ants, and beetles. Skip all the slow mid-river flats and focus strictly on fast, grassy banks and deep undercut structure. ***There are reports of a new tree down between Turah and Sha-Ron about half a mile above the confluence of Clark Fork and Blackfoot. Call the shop for more details 406.542.7411*** ***There are reports of a new tree down between Clinton and Turah. Call the shop for more details 406.542.7411***
